clue.text: The word just before this is a hybrid

parts.note: taken as written
a cross is an animal or plant bred from two different kinds

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about language: the word sitting just before this one is some sort of mongrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the grid itself: in the clue list, the heading printed just before clue 1 is the word that answers it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clue lists print the heading for this direction immediately above the first clue, so that heading is literally the preceding word.

clue.text: Take advantage of days after account is charged

indicators.note: after tells us the later pieces follow the account abbreviation in the answer

parts.note: ACC is a standard abbreviation for account
to use someone is to take advantage of them
D is the abbreviation for days

explanation.surface: Someone exploited a few days' grace on an account and ended up being prosecuted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be charged with a crime is to be formally accused of it, so the two past participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Religious leader to go on without end

indicators.note: without end asks us to drop the final letter of the word just clued

parts.note: to rabbit on is British slang for talking at tedious length

explanation.surface: A preacher is told to keep talking forever, a sermon that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'rabbit' or 'rabbit on' is informal British English for chattering on endlessly; cutting its last letter leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and teacher who leads a congregation, so he is a religious leader.

clue.text: Get word Edward is after beer that's robust

indicators.note: is after places the listening and the name behind the drink in the finished word

parts.note: stout is a dark, strong beer
to hear is to get word of something
Ted is a common short form of Edward

explanation.surface: News arrives that Edward is chasing a beer, presumably a strong one.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout-hearted means brave and resolute, a figurative sense of being robust in spirit.

clue.text: Group of pupils in favour of marks

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it
M is an abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A teacher's class votes in favour of the marks they have been given.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools a form is the class a pupil belongs to, a group taught together.

clue.text: Paper folding kit friend needed to support circular letter

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits underneath, so these come after the circular letter

parts.note: O is the round letter
a rig is a set of equipment or kit
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A craft kit for paper folding, with a friend helping to prop up a round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into decorative shapes.

clue.text: Possibly become empty after a month

indicators.note: after places the remaining letters behind the month in the answer

parts.note: May is a month of the year

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, keeping just its outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of become

explanation.surface: Perhaps something will be emptied out once a month has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe and possibly are synonymous adverbs, both expressing that something might be the case.

clue.text: Reportedly get money for small room

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so we want a word sounding like the one clued

parts.note: to sell something is to get money for it

explanation.surface: A rumour that someone is being paid to give up a tiny room.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery.

clue.text: Saddened daughter is given the job

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
taken as written
someone appointed has been given a post

explanation.surface: A parent is unhappy that their daughter got the job, oddly enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disappointed means feeling let down, a form of sadness when hopes are unmet.

clue.text: Bad smell round inside of container in US railway wagon

indicators.note: inside of means the first pieces are placed within the container word

parts.note: a case is a container
BO is body odour
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An unpleasant odour lingers inside an American freight wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: BO, body odour, is a crossword favourite for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A caboose is the guard's car at the rear of a North American freight train.

clue.text: Island in Med has head killed in a hostile manner

indicators.note: killing the head means cutting off the first letter of the word

parts.note: Sicily is the largest Mediterranean island

explanation.surface: A Mafia-flavoured scene: a Mediterranean island where the boss has been bumped off.
explanation.definitionFit: To act icily is to behave coldly and unfriendly, which is a hostile manner.

clue.text: Smallest fragment of lilac isn't to be arranged

indicators.note: to be arranged says the letters will be set out in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A florist notes that not even a sprig of lilac is going into the arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or particle, as in 'not a scintilla of evidence'.

clue.text: Beer available in local establishment

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the end of local runs into the start of establishment

explanation.surface: Beer on tap at the neighbourhood pub.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is a person's nearby pub, which makes the surface read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is a type of beer brewed with top-fermenting yeast.

clue.text: Scatter 500 piles all over the place

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: things all over the place are in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Five hundred heaps get knocked over and scattered everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel is to drive away or disperse, so it is a synonym of scatter as a verb.

clue.text: Second work managed by old singer

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
op. (opus) is a musical work
to run something is to manage it
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A second piece of music is run by an elderly vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest female or boy's voice range.

clue.text: A few months to get well

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the season between winter and summer
second meaning: a natural source of water rising from the ground

explanation.surface: It takes a few months to recover from an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get well' reads as recovering, but well is a noun here: a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The season lasts roughly three months, and a natural water source is also called by this word.

clue.text: Chap putting arm in jacket, perhaps

indicators.note: in places the limb within the word for chap

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a chap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man slides his arm into the sleeve of a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket is one example of an item of clothing, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Mountain ace getting record

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A top climber sets a record on a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: An alp is a high mountain, especially one in Switzerland.

clue.text: Something worth having — like TV?

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
a TV set

explanation.surface: A wry question whether a television counts as a valuable possession.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a valuable possession or useful quality, something worth having.

clue.text: Prompt about a rest

indicators.note: about means going around, so the prompt word surrounds the single letter

parts.note: a reminder is a prompt
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nudge to someone to take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the rest.

clue.text: Injure Epsom's first horse

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the racecourse name

parts.note: the initial letter of Epsom

explanation.surface: A warning about hurting the leading runner at Epsom.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is the English racecourse that hosts the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare is a female horse.

clue.text: Scandinavian introducing clubs for disco, say

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something inside, so the card suit goes within the nationality

parts.note: a Dane is a person from Denmark
C is the abbreviation for the card suit clubs

explanation.surface: A Dane shows a friend round the nightclubs, looking for a disco.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is one example of a dance, an event where people dance, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Box key is surplus to requirements

parts.note: to spar is to box in practice
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A spare key in a box is not needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spare is extra, more than is required.

clue.text: English join with queen returning in train

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the joined pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
to unite is to join
R is short for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: An Englishman joins the Queen on her journey home by train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' suggests the railway, but here it is a monarch's following.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a group of attendants, also called a train, accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Attempt to encircle Oman's capital city once

indicators.note: to encircle means to go round, so the attempt word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: capital means the head or initial letter of the country name

parts.note: the initial letter of Oman

explanation.surface: A bid to surround Muscat, the capital of Oman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oman's capital' looks like Muscat, but capital means its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy is the ancient city of the Trojan War, a city that no longer exists.

clue.text: Commercial trade unfortunately involves little volume

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so the small piece goes inside the jumbled letters
unfortunately suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
V is the abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: Commercial trade has sadly shrunk, with only a small volume of business.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert is a commercial, an advertisement broadcast or printed to sell something.
